questions.q: In `function onChange(control, oldValue, newValue, isLoading, isTemplate)`, what type are `oldValue` and `newValue`, even for a reference or numeric field?
options: Strings — always, regardless of the field's underlying type
Numbers for numeric fields, strings for everything else
GlideRecord objects
Booleans
questions.explain: onChange always passes oldValue and newValue as strings, which is why newValue == '1' is the safe comparison, not newValue === 1.

options: g_form.addErrorMessage is not a real API
It never returns false, so the platform has no signal to block the save
onSubmit cannot read field values with g_form.getValue
The condition should use === instead of ==
questions.explain: onSubmit only blocks the save when the function explicitly returns false. Showing a message alone doesn't stop anything.

questions.q: Why does onCellEdit fire in a way the other three client script types never do?
options: It only runs on mobile devices
It is the only type that runs on the server
It triggers on an inline cell edit in a list view, with no form ever opening
It replaces onLoad entirely in newer ServiceNow releases
questions.explain: onLoad, onChange, and onSubmit are all form-level hooks. onCellEdit is list-level — it fires when a user double-clicks a cell in a list to edit it inline.

questions.q: Given `function onCellEdit(sysIDs, table, oldValues, newValue, callback)`, what must the script do to actually allow or block the edit?
options: Return true or false from the function
Set g_form.setValue to the new value manually
Throw an exception to block the edit
Call callback(true) to allow it or callback(false) to block it
questions.explain: onCellEdit doesn't look at a return value. The edit stays pending until the script invokes the callback function with true or false.

questions.q: Why can't an onCellEdit script call g_form.addErrorMessage() to show a validation message?
options: g_form.addErrorMessage() is deprecated across the whole platform
There is no form in a list-view inline edit, so g_form isn't available — g_list is the equivalent
onCellEdit scripts can only run server-side, not client-side
g_form only works inside onSubmit
questions.explain: Because onCellEdit runs against a list, not a form, the form-specific g_form object doesn't exist in that context. Use g_list instead.
